sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Fayette County
sections.html:
Deeds for Fayette County property are recorded at the Recorder of Deeds office in the courthouse at 61 E Main Street, Uniontown, PA 15401. The office phone is 724-430-1238 and the fax is 724-430-1458.

Records here go back to 1784. Before that the area belonged to Westmoreland County. The office also records mortgages, releases, satisfaction pieces, plans, powers of attorney, leases, notary bonds and military discharges. DD-214 forms are the one record that isn't public.

For a seller, the recorder is the last stop. The deed signed at the closing table becomes the public record of the new owner only once this office stamps it, assigns an instrument number plus a volume and page, and prints the recording time on every page.

The office is open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., with the front counter shut from 12 to 1 each day. Recording follows the same pattern, so a deed that arrives during the lunch closure waits for the afternoon session.

  • Office hours: 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., closed 12 to 1.
  • Recording hours: 8 a.m. to noon and 1 p.m. to 4 p.m.

If you are delivering a closing package in person, arrive well before 4 p.m. and bring payment. All recording fees and transfer taxes are due at the time of recording.

sections.h2: What a deed must show to be accepted
sections.html:
A deed needs a typed parcel number, a proper notary acknowledgment and correct tax paperwork, or it comes back unrecorded. The county's recording requirements page lays out the rules, and most rejections come from small gaps in them.

  • A PIN (the tax assessment parcel number) must be typed on the first page. The Tax Assessment Office issues a UPI number for it before the document is recorded.
  • The acknowledgment must name the county, state and date, and the person or corporate officer appearing. It needs the notary's signature and commission expiration date. The acknowledgment date can't come before the date of the document. An embossed seal is now optional.
  • The deed must name the municipality, county and state where the land sits.
  • The written dollar amount must match the numerals on every deed and mortgage.
  • Grantee, mortgagee and assignee need a mailing address with ZIP code.
  • Any document that points back to an earlier mortgage must cite its book and page numbers, not a document number alone.
  • A re-recorded document has to explain why it is being recorded again.

Typing or writing on a notary stamp violates Pennsylvania notary law, the county says, so a smudged or altered stamp is a common reason for a bounce. Every document also needs a printed name so it can be returned to the right attorney or title company, along with a self-addressed stamped envelope unless the office will hold it for pickup.

The total is the base fee for the document type plus add-ons. Call 724-430-1238 and the office will quote the current deed figure. These are the add-ons that apply to a typical home sale.

Fayette County Recorder of Deeds add-on fees
Add-onAmount
UPI fee, per PIN number$20.00
Each page over 4$2.00
Each name over 4 (indexing)$0.50
Extra marginal notation$2.00
Copies in the office, per page$0.50
Copies by mail, per page$1.00
Certified copy$3.00 plus the copy cost

The UPI charge is per parcel, which matters on rural sales. A farm assembled from three tax parcels needs three PIN numbers certified, and each one carries the UPI fee.

Recording fees and realty transfer tax can go in one check made out to Fayette County Recorder of Deeds. The county fee schedule describes the transfer tax as 1% state plus 1% local.

The deed has to state the price paid, or it must carry a Statement of Value that explains why no tax is due. An original goes into the document as a page and a duplicate goes to the state. Questions about the tax can be emailed to the Department of Revenue realty transfer tax division at ra-bitrealtytransfertax@pa.gov.

When a property lies in more than one local taxing district, the deed must show whole-number percentages for the division of the local share. Buyer and seller are both liable for the tax, and the recorder passes the 1% state share to the Department of Revenue.

Index searches for most documents from 1950 to the present are free through the US Land Records site, though images are pay-per-access. Documents recorded before January 1, 2001 are also kept in books in the office, and public search stations in the Uniontown courthouse show the rest.

The recorder indexes by name, with the legal description and municipality, not by street address. For an address or parcel lookup, use the Tax Assessment property search or the Mapping Room at 724-430-1350, extension 229.

  • Archive Viewer indexes cover deeds and mortgages from 1950 to 1974, plans from 1791 to 1988 and agreements from 1854 to 1949.
  • Liens and judgments aren't filed here. The Prothonotary on the first floor of the courthouse handles them at 724-430-1272.
  • Subdivision plans are recorded in this office. Zoning questions go to Planning, Zoning and Community Development on the fourth floor at 724-430-1210.

sections.h2: Steps from closing to recorded deed
sections.html:
Here is the usual path. The deed is signed and notarized at closing. The closing agent gets the PIN certified through the Tax Assessment Office and types it on the first page. The package then goes to the Uniontown office with one check for fees and transfer tax, a printed return name and a self-addressed stamped envelope. Staff stamp it, assign the instrument number and record it.

If you are the seller, ask the closing agent when the package will be delivered. A deed that sits in an office drawer is not yet public record, and a rejected one has to be fixed and sent again.

sections.h2: Selling a house in Fayette County
sections.html:
Fayette County has an estimated 123,021 residents in 2025, down 4.5% from the April 2020 base. Owners occupy 72.4% of homes, and the median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 is $143,200. Median gross rent is $793, which matters if you are weighing a rental against a sale.

Uniontown, where the courthouse stands, anchors the county. A seller who wants a quick closing mainly needs a clean deed, a certified parcel number and a buyer whose title agent knows how the Uniontown office works. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting steps, but the deed still has to pass the same recording checks described above.

faqs.q: How much is the UPI fee in Fayette County?
faqs.a: The posted schedule shows $20.00 for each PIN number certified. A deed that covers two tax parcels therefore adds $40.00 to the recording bill.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed in Fayette County without a parcel number?
faqs.a: No. The county requires a PIN typed on the first page, and the Tax Assessment Office issues the UPI number before recording. A deed without it comes back unrecorded.

faqs.q: Can one check cover the recording fee and transfer tax in Fayette County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county allows fees and realty transfer tax in a single check payable to Fayette County Recorder of Deeds, as long as the amount is exact.

faqs.q: Does the Fayette County recorder search for liens?
faqs.a: No. Liens and judgments go through the Prothonotary's office in the courthouse at 724-430-1272. The recorder shows mortgages and whether they were satisfied.

faqs.q: Where do I get a copy of my recorded deed in Fayette County?
faqs.a: Visit the Uniontown office, where copies are $0.50 per page, or find the document through the US Land Records index. A certified copy costs $0.50 per page plus $3.00 for the certification.
